claims: Creator merges PRs without manually reviewing code, relying on agent-run verification
Creator: former big-tech engineer, startup with 50,000+ users and $100k+ ARR, ships ~30 PRs/day and 600+ PRs in 2026 so far (transcript garbled: '30, 600')
Browser-use/computer-use models are good enough to test the app instead of the human
Verification skills live in a 'gigantic skills folder' and teach models how to use each part of the app
Run pstack's create-verification-skill and maintain-verification-skill before every PR to keep testing instructions current
This is video 1 of 7; next video covers agents writing, reviewing, validating and merging code with no human
how_to_steps: For each area of your app, write a detailed verification skill (how to navigate, what to click, expected results) in a skills folder
When asking the model to change a part of the app, have it read the matching verification skill, run the test (browser/computer use) and confirm the change works
Before opening a PR, run pstack's 'create verification skill' to add instructions for new features and 'maintain verification skill' to update existing ones
Use Cursor cloud agent or Devin so the test run is recorded; review the screenshots/recording instead of the code
Merge when the recording/screenshots show the feature working

relevance.why: This is the exact leverage a solo, time-poor founder needs: move testing from the human to the agent via per-feature verification skills in the repo. Applies directly to Claude Code skills and to Claude Code's browser/computer-use tooling.

implement_score.why: Start now: add a /skills/verify-<feature>.md per app area, have Claude Code run it (Playwright/browser MCP) after each change and attach screenshots to the PR; add a pre-PR step that updates the skills. pstack itself is optional, the pattern is the value.
